preset.label: Washing machine, direct drive
preset.about: A wet load tumbled each way at 45 rpm, two rinses, then a spin to 1400 rpm: about half an hour

usage.said: 220 washes a year, what an energy label counts

why: 8 kg of dry laundry holds about as much again of water: 16 kg wet, half of it lifted on the wall of a 0.5 m drum and dropped at a time, which asks 9.8 N·m on average and as much again once a turn
a tumble of 11 s each way at 45 rpm with 3 s pauses, below the 60 rpm at which the laundry is held to the wall
10 minutes of washing and two rinses of 4, each followed by a drain at 600 or 800 rpm
the spin spreads the load at 90 rpm, holds 400 rpm while most of the water leaves, and holds 1400 rpm for 5 minutes
0.6 kg·m² for the drum and the wet load, 1 N·m for the bearings and the seal, and air and water drag of 0.012 N·m a rad/s, about 3 N·m at the top of the spin
an unbalance of 0.4 kg at the drum's radius once a turn, about what such a machine's control lets it spin with
preset.link: Driven directly on the motor shaft: the load's top speed of 1,400 rpm is 1,400 rpm at the motor, against your design speed of 3,000 rpm.

lines: the drive knows where the rotor is from the first instant, so it applies only the current the torque needs

checks.message: supply is 54% of the 600 V rating

junction peaks at 54 °C (52 to 60 °C across the thermal assumptions, the largest part of it from how the chips of the package heat each other, which the datasheet does not give), 90 °C below its rating
peak current 4.4 A against a 30 A rating

the operating point is outside the datasheet's data: turn-on energy: scaled linearly from 300 V test voltage to 325 V; above the test voltage real devices rise faster, by up to 3% more here (and 2 more, under data support)

braking returns 1810 J to the DC link, 961 J of it in one stretch of 15 s, at up to 90 W; a supply that cannot take it back needs at least 15400 µF on the link to stay under 480 V, or a braking resistor able to take 90 W
the motor current carries 0.0861 A of ripple, peak to peak, at the switching frequency: 19% of its 0.449 A peak
the DC-link capacitor carries 1.46 A rms of ripple at the switching frequency: its ripple-current rating has to be at least that. The supply's own ripple comes on top

if the drive stops switching at 1400 rpm, the motor's back-EMF is 910 V between lines, above the device's 600 V rating: the diodes would charge the link past it. This needs protection that shorts the motor or burns the energy, or a lower top speed

method.said: the motion is long beside the heatsink's time constant (5 min, an assumed one): the heatsink is followed from the air's temperature as it warms

taken: dead time taken as 1 µs, usual for an IGBT: the datasheet gives no turn-off times to work one out from. It takes from the voltage the stage can give. Give yours if it differs
heatsink heat capacity taken as 375 J/K, the usual for 0.8 K/W: it reaches 63% of its rise in 5 minutes. Give yours to replace it
